4Q136 f1:1.en: Which I command you today to love YHWH your God and to work with all your heart and with all your being. And I will give rain to your land in its season.
4Q136 f1:1.notes: Uncertain object marker and divine name suffix in position 9; uncertain divine name suffix in position 11; uncertain morphology in position 14. Phrase evidence applied for 'the rain your land' (positions 25-26), 'with all heart' (positions 15-17), and 'with all being' (positions 19-21).

4Q136 f1:2.en: And spring-rain, and you gathered its corn, and its wine, and its oil. And I gave its herb in your field to your cattle, and it ate and was sated. Take heed lest your heart be spacious, and you turn aside and serve.
4Q136 f1:2.notes: The translation follows the visible text and morphology, with two reconstructed particles (positions 1, 19) and one uncertain verb (position 19). The phrase 'take heed to' (positions 23-24) is supported by repeated evidence but not mandatory phrasing. No unlicensed elements were added.

4Q136 f1:3.en: Other gods and you bowed to them and it burned the anger of Yahweh on and he restrained the heavens and not it will be rain and the soil not it will yield produce and you perished in haste
4Q136 f1:3.notes: The phrase 'it burned the anger of Yahweh on' reflects high-confidence phrase evidence for positions 8-9-10. The sequence 'not it will be rain' follows repeated phrase evidence for positions 18-19-20, despite low support. Positions 25-26-27 use tentative 'it will yield produce' based on weak phrase evidence. The text has two reconstructions and one uncertain reading.

4Q136 f1:4.en: From upon the good land which Yahweh has given to you, and you shall put these words upon your heart and upon your soul, and you shall tie them for a sign upon your hand, and they will be for marks.
4Q136 f1:4.notes: Source contains reconstructed or uncertain text.

4Q136 f1:5.en: Between your eyes, and you shall teach them your sons to speak in your dwelling in the house, and in your walking in the way, and in your lying down, and in your arising. And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house.
4Q136 f1:5.notes: The phrase 'between your eyes' is a literal translation of the Hebrew, which may suggest a metaphorical meaning related to visibility or prominence. The phrase 'to speak in' is a dominant contextual rendering of the Hebrew 'לְדַבֵּר בְּ'. The phrase 'your dwelling in the house' is a possible interpretation of the Hebrew 'בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵית', which could also mean 'when you sit in the house'. The phrase 'in your walking in the way' is a dominant contextual rendering of the Hebrew 'בְּלֶכְתְּךָ בַדָּרֶךְ'. The phrase 'in your lying down' is a literal translation of the Hebrew 'בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ'. The phrase 'in your arising' is a literal translation of the Hebrew 'בְּקוּמֶךָ'. The phrase 'upon the doorposts of your house' is a dominant contextual rendering of the Hebrew 'עַל מְזוּזוֹת בֵּיתֶךָ'.

4Q136 f1:6.en: And in your gates, so your days and the days of your sons may be multiplied upon the land which YHWH swore to your ancestors to give to them, like the days of the heavens upon the earth. And he said, YHWH to Moses.
4Q136 f1:6.notes: Source contains reconstructed or uncertain text.

4Q136 f1:7.en: And Aaron, this is the regulation of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it. And no servant, man of livestock, or silver purchase shall eat of it. Then a sojourner and a hired laborer shall not eat of it. In a house one shall eat it, not outside.
4Q136 f1:7.notes: The translation follows the visible transcription and morphology, with phrase evidence guiding contextual disambiguation. Uncertainty remains in positions 17-18 (man of livestock) and 29 (preposition 'in'), where damage obscures the exact wording. The phrase 'in a house one' (positions 31-33) is supported by repeated evidence, though its exact syntax is unclear. The verb 'shall eat' is supplied for fluency where the source has only a negated form, following evidence-based reconstruction.

4Q136 f1:8.en: Take it out from the house from the flesh outside and the bone you shall not break in it. All the congregation of Israel shall make it. For he sojourns with you and made Passover to YHWH. Circumcise then every male and he will approach
4Q136 f1:8.notes: Uncertain reconstructions and damage affect 'make it' (position 18), 'Passover' (position 27), 'circumcise' (position 30), and 'every male' (position 32). Phrase evidence supports 'all the congregation of Israel' (positions 15-17), 'he sojourns with you' (positions 21-23), and 'a Passover to YHWH' (positions 27-29)

4Q136 f1:9.en: To make and be as the native-born of the land and the whole uncircumcised shall not eat in it. One instruction shall be to the native and to the sojourner who dwells in your midst. And they made all the people of Israel as he had commanded Yahweh (et) Moses and (et) Aaron.
4Q136 f1:9.notes: Positions 23, 35, 38: uncertain reconstruction. Positions 15, 28: untranslatable punctuation.

4Q136 f1:10.en: Thus they did. And it was on the very day that YHWH brought the Israelites out from the land of Egypt by divisions. And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying: Consecrate to me every firstborn, the firstborn.
4Q136 f1:10.notes: The phrase 'by divisions' is uncertain due to damage in the source text. The repetition of 'firstborn' at the end is preserved as in the source, though its exact syntax is unclear.

4Q136 f1:11.en: The whole womb in the sons of Israel, in mankind and in cattle, is his. And Moses said to the people, Remember the day, this one, that you went out from the land of Egypt, from a house of slaves, that by strength of hand YHWH brought you out.
4Q136 f1:11.notes: Uncertain elements: Moses (16), remember (20), the (22), day (23), in (28), from (29), earth (30), house (33).

4Q136 f1:12.en: From this, do not eat leaven. The day you go out in the month of Abib. And it was that Yahweh would bring you to the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, who swore to your ancestors to give.
4Q136 f1:12.notes: Uncertain reconstructions and damage affect 'month' (position 13), 'the' before 'Hittite' (position 26), and 'Hittite' (position 27). Phrase evidence supports 'the month of Abib' (positions 13-15), 'Yahweh into the land' (positions 21-23), and 'the land of the Canaanite[s]' (positions 23-25), among others. No recoverable text exists for the damaged final verb form (position 42).

4Q136 f1:13.en: to a land flowing of milk and honey you worked the work this in month this six days you will eat matzo and in day the seventh festival to YHWH
4Q136 f1:13.notes: positions 3, 4, 15, 19, 20, 32 are uncertain; positions 1, 14, 20 are reconstructed

4Q136 f1:14.en: He will eat the seven days and not it will be seen by you leaven and not it will be seen by you leaven in all your territory and you will tell to your son on that day saying because of
4Q136 f1:14.notes: The translation follows the visible text and morphology, preserving repetition and uncertainty. Phrase evidence supports 'the seven days' (positions 3-5), 'not it will be seen by' (positions 12-14), and 'leaven in all' (positions 15-17). The phrase 'in all your territory' (positions 16-18) is supported by repeated evidence. The verb 'you will tell' (position 21) is uncertain due to damage and low phrase support. The prepositional phrase 'to your son' (position 23) is supported by repeated evidence. The phrase 'on that day' (positions 25-27) is supported by high-confidence evidence. The infinitive construction 'saying because of' (positions 28-31) is supported by repeated evidence, though the final word is cut off.

4Q136 f1:15.notes: The translation follows the visible transcription and morphology, with phrase evidence informing the rendering of 'the law of YHWH' and 'a sign on hand.' The final 'that' reflects the particle 'because' (למען) followed by 'that' (כי), though the exact syntax is uncertain due to damage. No recoverable text survives for the final word, indicated by a lacuna in the source.

4Q136 f1:16.en: Strongly he brought you out, Yahweh, from Egypt. And keep the regulation, this, to the appointed time from days days.
4Q136 f1:16.notes: The translation includes two reconstructed words and one uncertain word. The phrase 'from days days' is a literal rendering of the repeated 'days' in the source, following the evidence precedence rules.
